records.name: Barbados
records.summary_text: Barbados demands real caution. Courts struck down the buggery laws in 2022; Barbados has an organised community (Equals, B-GLAD) and a functioning state. No LGR; modest social conservatism; tourist areas accustomed to diverse visitors.

sources.title: LGBTQ rights in Barbados
sources.claim_summary: Lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) people in Barbados do not possess the same legal rights as non-LGBT people. records.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
records.summary_text: Saint Kitts and Nevis demands real caution. Part of the Eastern Caribbean decriminalisation wave (2022 court ruling); tiny population, tourist economy, no documented anti-trans violence pattern; no LGR.

sources.title: LGBTQ rights in Saint Kitts and Nevis

records.name: Dominica
records.summary_text: Dominica demands real caution. High Court decriminalised same-sex relations in April 2024 (fourth Eastern Caribbean state); the old law had allowed forced psychiatric commitment. No LGR; small community; no documented anti-trans violence pattern.

records.name: Saint Lucia
records.summary_text: Saint Lucia demands real caution. The Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court struck down sodomy/gross-indecency laws in July 2025 (Randall Theodule v AG) — the region's most recent decriminalisation, welcomed by the IACHR. Saint Lucia has a relatively organised community (ECADE, United and Strong) and hosts Pride. No LGR.
